= Phase 3: Readiness Integration & Simplification
:author: AI Assistant
:revdate: 2026-02-08
:toc: left
:toclevels: 3
:icons: font

== Overview

Integration of readiness checks into manifests services and elimination of redundant architectural layers. This phase dramatically simplifies the systemd orchestration while preserving all functional guarantees.

This phase evolved through two sub-phases:

* *Phase 3*: Integrate readiness checks into manifests services via `ExecStartPost`
* *Phase 3.5*: Eliminate redundant targets that only waited for one service each

== Objectives

* Move readiness checks from separate services into manifests services
* Preserve fail-fast behavior using `ExecStartPost` hooks
* Eliminate the 5 separate ready services
* Question the value of targets with single dependencies
* Simplify dependency graph to direct service relationships
* Reduce total file count and code lines while maintaining correctness

== User Insight

During Phase 3 discussion, the user raised a critical architectural question:

[quote, User]
____
so I think the target in systemd are designed when we have to wait for multiple services in a stage right ? do we have such a case really ?
____

*Analysis*: Systemd targets are coordination points where multiple contributing services synchronize before dependent services proceed. In our case:

* `rke2lab-runtime-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-runtime-ready.service` (1:1)
* `rke2lab-storage-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-storage-ready.service` (1:1)
* `rke2lab-networking-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-networking-ready.service` (1:1)
* `rke2lab-replication-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-replication-ready.service` (1:1)
* `rke2lab-mesh-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-mesh-ready.service` (1:1)
* `rke2lab-server-ready.target` - Only waited for `rke2lab-server-ready.service` (1:1)

*Conclusion*: All targets were redundant. A target with only one dependency provides no value - just use direct service dependencies.

*Exception*: `rke2lab-flox-builds-complete.target` coordinates multiple parallel `rke2lab-flox-build@*.service` instances, so it's legitimate and retained.

== Phase 3: Readiness Integration

=== Changes Made

==== Modified Manifests Services (5 files)

Added `ExecStartPost` directives to integrate readiness checks:

.*rke2lab-runtime-manifests.service*
[source,systemd]
----
[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/srv/host/scripts.d/rke2lab-manifests-install.sh runtime
ExecStartPost=/srv/host/scripts.d/rke2lab-layer-ready.sh runtime
----

.*rke2lab-storage-manifests.service*
[source,systemd]
----
[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/srv/host/scripts.d/rke2lab-manifests-install.sh storage
ExecStartPost=/srv/host/scripts.d/rke2lab-openebs-ready.sh
----

.*rke2lab-networking-manifests.service*
[source,systemd]
----
[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/srv/host/scripts.d/rke2lab-manifests-install.sh networking

==== Deleted Services (5 files)

[source,bash]

git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-runtime-ready.service
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-storage-ready.service
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-networking-ready.service

These services became redundant since their only job was to run the readiness script, now done via `ExecStartPost`.

*make.d/incus/scripts/rke2lab-activate.sh*

----
-  rke2lab-runtime-ready.service \

=== Results

.*Simplification*
* 5 fewer service files
* ExecStartPost provides equivalent fail-fast behavior
* Clearer: readiness check is part of manifests service lifecycle

.*Preserved Guarantees*
* Readiness scripts still execute after manifests apply
* Non-zero exit code from ExecStartPost fails the service
* Dependent services still wait for readiness (via `After=`)

== Phase 3.5: Target Elimination

=== Analysis

After readiness integration, we still had 6 targets acting as pass-through layers:

[source]
----
service.service → ready.target → next-service.service
----

Each target only waited for one service, providing no coordination value. Direct dependencies are simpler:

[source]
----
service.service → next-service.service
----

=== Changes Made

==== Deleted Targets (6 files)

[source,bash]
----
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-runtime-ready.target
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-storage-ready.target
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-networking-ready.target
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-replication-ready.target
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-mesh-ready.target
git rm -f make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-server-ready.target
----

==== Updated Service Dependencies

Changed all services from target-based to service-based dependencies:

.*rke2lab-storage-manifests.service*
[source,diff]
----
 [Unit]
 Description=RKE2 Lab Storage Layer Manifests
-After=rke2lab-runtime-ready.target
-Wants=rke2lab-runtime-ready.target
+After=rke2lab-runtime-manifests.service
+Wants=rke2lab-runtime-manifests.service
----

.*rke2lab-networking-manifests.service*
[source,diff]
----
 [Unit]
 Description=RKE2 Lab Networking Layer Manifests
-After=rke2lab-storage-ready.target
-Wants=rke2lab-storage-ready.target
+After=rke2lab-storage-manifests.service
+Wants=rke2lab-storage-manifests.service
----

Similar changes for:
* `rke2lab-replication-manifests.service` → After `networking-manifests`
* `rke2lab-mesh-manifests.service` → After `replication-manifests`
* `rke2lab-gitops-manifests.service` → After `mesh-manifests`
* `rke2lab-tekton-pipelines-manifests.service` → After `mesh-manifests`

==== Updated Drop-in Configurations

.*make.d/incus/systemd/rke2lab-gitops-manifests.service.d/10-manifests-install.conf*
[source,diff]
----
 [Unit]
-After=rke2lab-mesh-ready.service
-Wants=rke2lab-mesh-ready.service
+After=rke2lab-mesh-manifests.service
+Wants=rke2lab-mesh-manifests.service
----

=== Results

.*Architectural Simplification*
* No indirection through targets
* Direct `service → service` dependencies
* Easier to trace boot flow
* Clearer what blocks what

.*Files Eliminated*
* 6 target files deleted
* Net reduction: ~80 lines of systemd configuration

=== Preserved Guarantees

✅ *Boot Ordering*
* Service chain maintained: runtime → storage → networking → replication → mesh
* Dependencies explicit via `After=` and `Wants=`

✅ *Fail-Fast Behavior*
* `ExecStartPost` fails the service if readiness check returns non-zero
* Dependent services block on failed service (same as before)

✅ *Readiness Validation*
* All readiness scripts still execute
* Timing: after manifests applied, before service marked complete

== Lessons Learned

=== Systemd Architecture

.*When to use targets*
* Targets are for coordinating *multiple* services into a logical checkpoint
* 1:1 relationships (one service → one target) are unnecessary indirection
* Use direct service dependencies for linear chains

.*ExecStartPost semantics*
* Runs after main ExecStart completes successfully
* Non-zero exit fails the entire service unit
* Perfect for post-condition validation (readiness checks)
* Equivalent fail-fast behavior to separate dependent service

=== Refactoring Strategy

* Start with inventory and analysis (Phase 1)
* Make incremental, testable changes (Phases 2, 3)
* Be open to user insights that reshape the plan (Phase 3.5)
* Validate at each step (grep searches, git status)

=== Collaboration

* User brought architectural insight about target necessity
* Agent adapted plan based on that insight
* Result: even better simplification than originally planned
